data.cultural_impact: The name "Ishithansh" is derived from Sanskrit language, a classical language of the Indian subcontinent. The name Ishithansh is a unique and beautiful combination of two meaningful words in Hinduism - Ishita and Ansh. Ishita signifies the Goddess of Grace, and Ansh means the essence or presence. In Hindu culture, the significance of the name Ishithansh would be looked upon with reverence towards the graceful presence of the deity or the divine power. This name would be considered auspicious, and the bearer of the name may be seen as someone who embodies the grace and essence of the Supreme Being.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Ishithansh" is deeply rooted in Hindu philosophy. The name "Ishita" represents the divine feminine energy, which is the source of all creation and the nurturer of all beings. The name "Ansh" signifies the essence or presence of the supreme reality, which is beyond form and attributes. The name Ishithansh signifies the presence and grace of the divine feminine energy in human life. It is a constant reminder of the mere illusion of separateness and the profound interconnectedness of all beings with the supreme reality. The bearer of this name is considered to be eternally connected to the divine grace and essence of the universe. The name "Ishithansh" is a sacred symbol of spiritual growth and enlightenment. It represents a deep reverence for the divine grace and a constant striving to align one's thoughts, words, and actions with the divine will. The name is a powerful reminder of the ultimate reality and the deep spiritual significance of human existence.

historical_references.reference: Ishithansh is mentioned in the ancient Hindu epic Mahabharata, specifically in the Bhagavad Gita, where it is referred to as one of the many names of Lord Vishnu.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is a Sanskrit epic that was likely composed between 400 and 200 BCE, and the Bhagavad Gita is a part of this epic, in which the god Vishnu speaks to the warrior Arjuna.

historical_references.reference: Ishithansh is also mentioned in the Puranas, particularly in the Shiva Purana, where it is described as one of the many aspects of Shiva, representing the power of creation and preservation.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a set of 18 Hindu scriptures, composed between 500 and 1000 CE, that provide mythological and historical narratives about various Hindu deities.
